about: Lab scenarios for the console's Lab tab (BACKLOG B13). A wish is the game's own cheat prompt (Ctrl+W, or Shift+W for a menu; verified in Commands.xml). The prompt takes ONE line: paste or type one wish at a time. Use a throwaway character with the AI paused. Wish kinds: 'blueprint' = the creature or item name typed alone (verified in game 2026-10-08: SecurityTurret spawned one; the 'spawn:' prefix did NOT work, the log said Unknown blueprint); 'command' = a named wish. Confidence: 'verified' = seen working in the game, 'documented' = labelled in the game's WishCommands.xml, 'named' = the string is recognised by the wish handler but its effect was not read.

scenarios.title: Turret nest
scenarios.why: Test the turret doctrine (HANDOFF issue 77) without waiting for a run that meets one: a turret listed as an enemy, shot with Lase, never rested in front of.
setup: Pause the AI and find open floor with at least 8 clear tiles in one direction.

Wishes put a creature in the first empty cell NEXT TO YOU: there is no distance setting. So: turn godmode on, spawn the turret, walk the distance you want (5 or 6 tiles, in its line of sight), turn godmode off, then Engage the AI.
Copy and enter the lines in order, one at a time (the Copy button gives the next one each click): godmode, the turret, then walk, then godmode again.

wishes.note: turn it ON first so the turret's first shots cannot hurt you while you walk away ('Toggle godmode' in the game's menu; not yet seen working by us) WARNING (ENGINE_INTERNALS 14.36): godmode also makes EVERY damage event on anything but you 999, and it stays on in the running client even when you load another character: turn it OFF before you judge any damage, and restart the game when the lab ends.
verified in game: one musket turret appeared (level 15, 5 HP), next to you

after you have walked 5 or 6 tiles away: the same wish again turns it OFF. Do not forget, or the test proves nothing WARNING (ENGINE_INTERNALS 14.36): godmode also makes EVERY damage event on anything but you 999, and it stays on in the running client even when you load another character: turn it OFF before you judge any damage, and restart the game when the lab ends.

scenarios.title: Grenade lab: poison gas cloud (BACKLOG B33)
scenarios.why: Measure what a poison gas grenade does: how big the cloud gets, how long it lasts, how far it reaches and what it does to a creature standing at 4 and 5 tiles. The mod now exports every gas cell near him (`gas_cells`) and the brain writes `memory/gas_log.jsonl`, one line per turn.
setup: Take a SNAPSHOT first (Control tab). Go to a flat OPEN area (no walls within 8 tiles) and pause the AI. Turn godmode ON for the first runs (it keeps the poison from killing him; the cloud is still measured).
Wish for the grenade (below). It lands on a cell next to you: pick it up, and put it in the thrown-weapon slot if you like.
Walk so that the target cell is exactly the distance you want from you (4 tiles first, then 5), in a straight line in the open. Note the distance in the capture note.
In PowerShell: New-Item D:\QudAI\memory\lab_hold.flag -ItemType File   (this makes the brain stand still and log; delete the file when the run is over: Remove-Item D:\QudAI\memory\lab_hold.flag)
Throw the grenade yourself at the target cell with the game's throw command (still paused). Then Engage the AI with one Shift+Space wait: from now on every turn is logged and he stands still.

Let about 30 turns pass, then Capture logs with a note like 'poison gas mk I, thrown at distance 4, open ground'. Then delete the flag file, pause, and repeat at distance 5. Repeat once with the grenade wished as PoisonGasGrenade2.

wishes.note: ON for the first runs; OFF for one run at distance 6 to see the damage WARNING (ENGINE_INTERNALS 14.36): godmode also makes EVERY damage event on anything but you 999, and it stays on in the running client even when you load another character: turn it OFF before you judge any damage, and restart the game when the lab ends.
the mark I grenade (density 40); the brain's item logic calls it 'poison gas grenade mk I'; untried as a wish: if it does not spawn, try 'poison gas grenade mk I'
the mark II grenade (density 80), for the second series

scenarios.title: Zone-hop lab: do hostiles follow through an edge or stairs, what a frozen zone does, and does Lase recharge while away (ENGINE_INTERNALS 14.46)
scenarios.why: The engine code says only ONE zone is active, hostiles are never carried across an edge or stairs (only the player's party is), a left zone is frozen, and Lase recharges on his own turns wherever he is (14.45, 14.46). That was read, not seen. Three possible rules depend on it: retreat to the nearest exit and cross it, a peek-and-leave descent into deeper strata, and leaving a fight to recharge Lase. This lab answers four questions in the game itself: (1) does anything follow him across an edge or down stairs, adjacent or not; (2) is the pack where he left it when he comes back, after 60 and after 300 rounds; (3) how many charges does Lase regain in 60 rounds away; (4) who acts first on the return, and does the pack get a free hit.
setup: Use a THROWAWAY Esper (it has Lase; any build works for questions 1 and 2) and take a SNAPSHOT first (Control tab). Pause the AI for the whole lab: you play by hand. Turn godmode ON so the snapjaws cannot kill him (do not fight them; with godmode on his own hits would also be 999). WARNING (ENGINE_INTERNALS 14.36): godmode stays on in the running client; turn it OFF for series E and restart the game when the lab ends.

SERIES A, an EDGE. Walk to the edge of an open surface zone (a cell on x 0 or 79, or y 0 or 24) with no water or walls beside the edge cell. Wish three Snapjaw Scavengers, one wish at a time (below); they land next to you. Take a screenshot (their cells). Press Capture logs with the note 'zone-hop A1: three adjacent at the edge'.

Step across the edge. Look at the new zone at once: is any snapjaw with you (count them, screenshot)? Press Capture logs 'zone-hop A2: just crossed, N followed' (the capture's exchange_last_state.json lists every creature in view with its zone).

SERIES C, the Lase charge, before the rest: fire Lase into empty space until the ability list shows 'Lase (1 charges)' (it shows 'Lase (4 charges)' when full at mutation level 1). Write down the charges. Then REST in the new zone for exactly 60 rounds (the game's wait command: the `Z` menu or the wait key; count the rounds, `[unverified]` which key your game uses). Press Capture logs 'zone-hop C: rested 60 rounds, Lase N charges' and write the charges you see.

Step back across the edge. Screenshot the pack at once: same cells as in A1, or different? Press Capture logs 'zone-hop A3: back after 60 rounds'. Count the rounds until the first snapjaw acts (the first time one moves or hits).

SERIES D, a LONG absence. Cross the edge again, rest 300 rounds (food and water are fine for this), come back and screenshot the pack: still the same cells as in A1? Capture 'zone-hop D: back after 300 rounds'. If they moved, the zone does catch up on thaw (note by how much).

SERIES B, STAIRS. Find stairs down (any cave or ruin entrance; the brain's console prints known stairs, or use the entrance of the zone where the Esper delved). Stand next to the stairs on the upper level, wish three Snapjaw Scavengers, screenshot, Capture 'zone-hop B1', take the stairs down, check who came (B2), come back up after 60 rounds and screenshot (B3). Note whether you arrive ON the stairs and who is next to them.

SERIES E, ARRIVAL (optional, godmode OFF, full HP, ONE snapjaw only): repeat the edge crossing with one Snapjaw Scavenger adjacent, come back after 60 rounds and write down HP at the return and after the next two turns: who acts first on arrival, and does a creature that was adjacent when you left hit you before you can act? Then restart the game.

wishes.note: ON for series A to D; OFF for series E. WARNING (ENGINE_INTERNALS 14.36): it also makes EVERY damage event on anything but you 999 and stays on in the running client even when you load another character: restart the game when the lab ends.

Lase charges before and after 60 rounds away (the ability name in exchange_last_state.json abilities); expected 1 charge back per 15 rounds at Willpower 16, so 4 charges after 60 rounds, faster with higher Willpower (ENGINE_INTERNALS 14.45)
